newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt receives 26 bids for airports.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt receives 26 bids for airports.

text.p: The Australian government said on Monday it had received 26 expressions of interest for the sale of Brisbane, Perth and Melbourne airports.

"Expressions of interest closed last Thursday and I'm pleased to tell the house (of representatives) that at that time some 26 bids or expressions of interest were received in respect of the three airports," Finance Minister John Fahey told parliament.

"Those expressions of interest will be evaluated against the government's objectives for the sale of those airports and ultimately a certain number of bidders will proceed or progress to stage two," he said.
"That list will be drawn up shortly."
Fahey emphasised that price would not be the sole deciding factor on which groups made it on to the government's short list.
A spokesman for Fahey told Reuters last Thursday that formal bidding was scheduled to start later this month and was likely to close in late January.
The Australian government won parliamentary approval for the A$2.0 billion sale of the country's main airports in September.
In the same month, it advertised nationally for bidders for 50-year leases for the first round of airports - Brisbane, Perth and Melbourne.
Adelaide airport may also be sold in 1996/97.

The remaining airports are scheduled to be sold in 1997/98 with the possible exception of Sydney airport and the planned second airport. The sale of the two Sydney airports is being delayed as a result of noise and environment studies.
